title.en: A mustard seed and a lesson

text.en: A grieving mother goes to the Buddha. His answer teaches a lesson about death.

Kisa Gotami's only son had died. In her grief she carried the dead child from house to house, asking for medicine.
A kind man advised her to go to the Buddha, who could help her.
The Buddha asked her to bring a handful of mustard seed from a house where no one had died.
She went from door to door, but every house had lost a loved one, so she found no such house.
She sat at the roadside watching the lights of the city flicker up and go out, and thought of the fate of men.
She understood that death is common to all and that she had been selfish in her grief.
The Buddha explained that life is troubled and brief, and there is no means by which those born can avoid dying.
The sermon teaches us to accept death and to overcome selfish sorrow by thinking of others.

problem.en: Kisa Gotami visited 5 houses each day for 3 days. How many houses?

why.en: She found no house without death.

prompt.en: What lesson did Kisa Gotami learn?

requiredIdeas.en: Her grief was shared by many
Selfish sorrow must give way to compassion

commonMisconceptions.en: Thinking the Buddha refused to help

points.en: Kisa Gotami lost her only son.
The Buddha asked for a mustard seed.
No house was free of death.
